summary: Native delivery connectors authenticate their role with a kernel peer generation and a bootstrap witness; native harness-event publication requires the same custody.

replay.detail: Graph replay and projections are unchanged.

schema.detail: Fresh native wrapper launches write a local process-generation bootstrap witness. No replicated claim schema or database migration changes.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: Native bind, subscribe/repair, receipts, attachment and harness-event publication require authenticated connector custody, following #2315 O1a and #4107. OMP/Pi extensions register their exact connector from the trusted provider generation before releasing startup. Session/sequence remain freshness fences. Boot-ID-less PTY records retain matching start-token compatibility without relaxing role proof.

downtime.detail: Already-bound live channels retain their exact persisted lease, kernel process generation and provider ownership through daemon restart and driver adoption. No fleet-wide harness restart is required.

manual.detail: Fresh launches establish the witness automatically. An older generation without a witness can retain its existing exact live custody but cannot acquire new native custody or promote to a different ownership sequence through that continuation path.

recovery.detail: Existing mailbox capabilities and provider state remain usable by previous builds. New local launch-witness files do not alter replicated state.
